name: Upper Navarrese Basque

ancestors.notes: Upper Navarrese uses the standard Basque grapheme base but exhibits systematic phonological reduction driven by Spanish contact, particularly in sibilant and lateral distinctions.

notes: Upper (High) Navarrese (Goi-Nafar). Navarrese Basque of the Pamplona basin and northern Navarre. VALIDATED and CORRECTED against Hualde, Lujanbio & Zubiri (2010), an Illustration of the IPA of Goizueta Basque, a conservative High Navarrese variety. Corrections vs. the prior draft: (1) the three-way sibilant contrast /s̻ s̺ ʃ/ (and matching affricates) is FULLY STABLE in this dialect group — the neutralisations run further west, in Gipuzkoan and Biscayan, not in Navarrese (Hualde et al. 2010: 119); the earlier claim of an apical/laminal merger to a single [s] here was unsourced and has been removed. (2) Aspiration (/h/) is absent: /h/ was lost in these varieties (Goizueta has no /h/; Hualde et al. 2010: 113 fn.1; Hualde 2018: 2). (3) Incipient yeísmo — the palatal lateral /ʎ/ delateralising to the palatal approximant [ʝ]~[j] — is documented and in progress, matching the parallel Spanish development (Hualde et al. 2010: 120). Voiced stops /b d ɡ/ are approximants [β ð ɣ] intervocalically (2010: 116). Some High Navarrese varieties (Goizueta) additionally show lexically contrastive pitch-accent (2010: 113, 123). Spanish contact is heavy in the Pamplona-basin sub-varieties, which are highly endangered. STRESS: the spec states "stress": false and does not take the Batua [+2] block of eu. Hualde (2022: 84, Table 2) gives Goizueta-Oiartzun, the variety this spec is validated against, a tonal system: "[+2H]" for unmarked words and "[+1H], [+1L], [+ L]" for the exceptions. Hualde (2022: 80, note 5) places part of Upper Navarre on the other side of the Western-Central vs Eastern isogloss: the change [+2] > [–2] "extended to the Baztan Valley but not to Bortziriak, leaving the village of Arantza on the western side of the isogloss". The area therefore holds a tonal [+2] system and a penultimate [–2] system, the H and L accents are lexical, and the spelling marks none of this. No single block can be written from these sources.
